statement: For δ>1 the discrete spectrum on Hχ is the critical-line zero ordinates in iR only, with multiplicity min(actual zero order, largest integer strictly below (1+δ)/2).

For a positive-characteristic global field, the cutoff trace identity on compactly supported test functions is equivalent to RH for every Grössencharakter L-function. The archimedean discussion instead changes the cutoff.

For E satisfying the theorem’s entire-function, no-real-zero, strict Hermite–Biehler, unit-modulus shift and vertical monotonicity hypotheses, nonnegative real shift form on the simultaneous translate domain forces Im(w)=-1/2 and the stated derivative sign. The paper reports a negative sign for the natural xi model.

For W analytic and zero-free in the upper half-plane, a kernel-translation linear operator on F(W) with nonnegative real numerical range forces continuation to Im(z)>-1/2 and a nonnegative quotient real part there. The paper reports a negative quotient real part in the natural reciprocal-xi model.

For fixed ω0≥0, zero-freeness in Re(s)>1/2+ω0 is equivalent to meromorphic innerness for all ω>ω0. For each fixed positive ω innerness is equivalent to the stated full-domain arithmetic Mellin convolution conditions.

Explicit determinant-ratio canonical Hamiltonian construction assumes ω>1. The stated weaker compressed-kernel conclusions include Hilbert–Schmidt and invertibility for ω>1/2 and compact self-adjointness for ω>0.
Eigenvalues of the transpose on the continuous dual of the nuclear Fréchet quotient equal the zeros of the meromorphic completed zeta, with algebraic multiplicities equal to zero orders.

For all f in the specified test algebra the signed Mellin spectral sum equals the virtual character and sum of local distributions, with pole orders positive and zero orders negative. Density in the proof is density of convolutions of compactly supported smooth functions in the test algebra.
Positivity of the explicit-formula distribution on W is stated to be equivalent to the conjunction of RH and Artin’s conjecture for all L_k(χ,s).
